title: A tweakable registry
description:
Build `Tweakables`, the registry behind the debug menu. It holds integer, floating-point and boolean variables by name.

- `addInt(name, int* value, min, max)`, `addFloat(name, float* value, min, max)`, `addBool(name, bool* value)` register a variable. Registering a name again replaces the old entry.
- `set(name, text)` parses `text` for that variable's type and stores it, **clamped** into its range: integers with `std::stoi`-like rules (the whole text must be a number), floats likewise, booleans from `"true"`/`"false"`/`"1"`/`"0"`/`"on"`/`"off"`. It returns a message: `"name = value"` on success (integers as digits, floats with `std::to_string`-like default formatting is not required: use `std::format("{}", v)`, booleans as `true`/`false`), `"unknown: name"` for an unknown name, or `"bad value: text"` if the text cannot be parsed. On failure the variable is unchanged.
- `get(name)` returns the current value as text in the same format, or `std::nullopt` for an unknown name.
- `names()` returns all names, sorted.

```
int sight = 8;  addInt("monster.sight", &sight, 1, 30)
set("monster.sight", "50")   -> "monster.sight = 30"    (clamped)
set("monster.sight", "lots") -> "bad value: lots"       (sight still 30)
```
hints: Store each entry as a small struct holding its kind (an `enum class Kind { Int, Float, Bool }`), a pointer for each kind (only the one that matches is used) and its limits, in a `std::map<std::string, Entry>` so the names come out sorted. A `switch` on the kind then picks the right parsing and formatting.
After a successful `set`, build the message from `get`, so both use the same format.
lessonTitle: A Debug Menu Inside the Game
